speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe when the swelling in your right knee started and if you experienced any recent trauma or injury?

speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does your son have a history of excessive bleeding from minor cuts, frequent bruising, or prolonged bleeding after vaccinations? Has he ever experienced pain or swelling in other joints, such as his elbows or ankles?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Swelling of the right knee. I also have No recent trauma or injury, Familial history of similar symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the bleeding history question apply to your son, or are you responding as the patient? Please clarify if the child has experienced excessive bleeding or bruising.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: The parents report no known allergies, normal birth and developmental history for the child.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: ACT: 52.0 s (prolonged), PT: 14.0 s, Thrombin time: < 2 seconds deviation from control

speaker: Doctor
text: The prolonged ACT with a normal PT suggests a factor VIII or IX deficiency. REQUEST TEST: Factor VIII and Factor IX levels

speaker: Doctor
text: Since Factor VIII and IX levels are normal, I need to rule out other coagulation disorders. REQUEST TEST: Factor VII, XI, and XII levels, as well as von Willebrand factor antigen and activity.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal coagulation profile, I suspect a non-hemophilic arthropathy or an inflammatory condition. Does the knee feel warm to the touch, and has your son had any recent fevers, rashes, or joint stiffness in the morning?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, rash, or recent illnesses.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since inflammatory and common bleeding disorders are ruled out, I suspect a hemostasis disorder not covered by the standard panel. REQUEST TEST: Platelet Function Assay and Factor XIII activity level

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Platelet Function Assay: NORMAL READINGS, Factor XIII activity level: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text: With hemostasis and common inflammatory causes ruled out, I need to evaluate for metabolic arthropathies like gout or pseudogout, or structural issues. REQUEST TEST: Joint aspiration for crystal analysis and inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP).

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Joint aspiration: Fluid is bloody (hemarthrosis), no crystals identified. ESR: Normal, CRP: Normal

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of spontaneous hemarthrosis with a normal standard coagulation profile and normal Factor VIII/IX levels strongly suggests a rare clotting factor deficiency, such as Factor XI deficiency, which is often associated with a family history of bleeding disorders. DIAGNOSIS READY: Hemophilia A or B variant (likely mild or atypical) or Factor XI deficiency
